_README: Verdicts for rows in FRICTION.md's GENERATED half, which the triage script
cannot know on its own — it reads telemetry, and telemetry does not record
whether anyone fixed anything.
Without this file every generated row said 'untested' forever. That was a
known limitation and then became a defect: after 4.21.2 and 4.26.0 the
table was still presenting resolved work as open candidates, and one
finding's own text opened with 'RESOLVED IN 4.26.0' beside a hard-coded
untested. A triage file that misreports its own state costs more than one
with gaps in it.
Verdict vocabulary — the three from FRICTION.md's preamble, plus one:
confirmed  — reproduced here; safe to act on
refuted    — tested here and did not hold. The row STAYS, marked refuted
untested   — plausible, unverified; must not reach a tool description
by-design  — not a defect: the tool saw a call it knew was wrong and
refused it. Recorded because calling a working guard an
untested candidate is as wrong as calling a fixed bug one,
and these rows are otherwise re-investigated every pass.
Matching. Failure rows are grouped by (tool, signature), so a verdict names
the tool and either `signature` (exact) or `signatureContains` (substring of
the normalised signature — note ids and numbers are already collapsed to
<n> and quoted values to '<v>'). Findings are keyed by their `at` epoch,
which is unique, with `tool` as a guard against a mistyped key.
`resolvedIn` is the version that fixed it. `resolvedAt` is the epoch that
version shipped: the generator flags any row still occurring AFTER that
date, so a verdict claiming a fix that did not hold shows up as a warning
rather than quietly reassuring everybody. Omit resolvedAt only when there
is nothing to re-check (by-design rows).
Entries whose rows are no longer in the log are reported by the generator
so they can be pruned. Do not delete a `refuted` entry — that is the one
this whole file exists to preserve.

failures.note: A bare 404 naming neither the device nor the property. The tool now re-reads the device on 404 and says which of the two is missing, listing the properties that exist; HC3HttpError carries the method and path. New occurrences will not match this signature.
Same bare 404. The opening device read is the tool's only unguarded request, so every one of these was a device that does not exist; it now says so.
Reported as HC3 refusing a `type` change specifically, with the same device accepting topLevel={visible:true}. Not isolated here.

The endpoint is refused on 5.210.12 for add and delete, single and multi, on QuickApps of two types AND on non-QuickApp device 3385 — whose interfaces and `modified` timestamp were byte-identical after both arms. Catalogued in KNOWN_DEAD_ENDPOINTS.md; the tool now carries it. Not fixed, because there is nothing here to fix: two of the seven are this project's own probe.

`content` omitted. HC3 rejected the create from inside its Lua engine, naming engine.lua rather than the missing argument. create_scene now supplies a body that subscribes to nothing and reports contentDefaulted.
`conditions` sent as a structure rather than a Lua source string. Refused locally now, with the Lua to send instead printed in the error.

The candidate paths omitted a segment: user device icons live at /assets/userIcons/devices/User<N>/. The tool's own error text asserted they were not served under any /assets path, which was a wrong negative, and a unit test pinned that assertion in place.

The schema's `required` listed base64/mime/category while the handler refused a device upload without deviceTemplate, so obeying the schema guaranteed the refusal. `required` is now mime/category with the dependent requirement expressed in schema.
The guard working: HC3 rejects roomId=0 on creation, and this refuses before the call.
Argument guard refusing a malformed call before it reaches HC3.

failures.signature: modify_device requires at least one of topLevel or properties with at least one field.

failures.note: Refusing to overwrite, and naming set_quickapp_variable as the way to update.
The pre-check working. HC3 silently accepts and drops invalid actions on QuickApps with an empty actions map, so this refusal is the only signal a caller gets.
A stale or mis-indented `old` refused with nothing written. Working as intended, though a run of these on one file usually means the caller is holding an out-of-date copy.
Not a defect in this tool — it is this tool catching HC3 accepting a write and storing something else. The underlying HC3 behaviour is the finding; each instance is worth reading on its own.

findings.note: Filed for the record by its own author, who noted it was already resolved. get_icon and upload_icon return a content hash.
The wrong-negative in get_icon's own error text. See the failures entry for the same defect.
Not a finding: the `statedir-check` self-test, filed to prove the finding channel survives a restart. Kept so nobody re-investigates it as a defect.
`content` documented as optional; omitting it drew a Lua-engine 400 about a nil `conditions`. create_scene now supplies an empty body that subscribes to nothing and reports contentDefaulted.

Settled 15 Aug by scripts/probe-uicallbacks.mjs. A real tap ALWAYS dispatches to UIAction positionally, whatever uiCallbacks registers; only call_ui_event honours the registered name and passes an event table. This report was right and this file's own model was wrong. Consequences applied to call_ui_event and modify_device descriptions.

Client-side, no server fix available: a tool going unreachable mid-session is the documented stale-schema symptom — schemas cache at connect and a reconnect may not refresh them. Recorded rather than fixed.
Settled 1 Sep on device 3385: the refusal is blanket, not per-interface, per-direction or per-device-class. Endpoint catalogued in KNOWN_DEAD_ENDPOINTS.md and the tool now carries it.
The three-variant isolation in this report was correct. The missing device-class arm was run on 3385 on 1 Sep and agreed.

Settled 15 Aug by scripts/probe-uicallbacks.mjs, twelve cells through the tool against eighteen real taps. The tool is more generous than reality on BOTH axes. Its own description now says so, and modify_device's end-to-end guarantee was withdrawn.
The second device type and fifth recorded failure, which is what made the pattern worth settling.

No tool composited images, so a badged icon had to leave as base64 and be re-typed back. upload_icon now takes an `overlay`; both images resolve gateway-side and nothing passes through the conversation.

Settled 1 Sep by scripts/probe-scene-variables.mjs on scene 670. All four REST spellings return 501 with an empty body — and so does a deliberately nonsensical sub-path on the same scene, which is the control that makes the result mean something: this is an unrouted path, not a feature that exists and refuses. The scene-variable tool is UNBUILDABLE, not unbuilt; the gap is struck rather than carried. Says nothing about fibaro.setSceneVariable, which never goes through REST.

Settled 1 Sep by scripts/probe-ios-device-by-id.mjs. GET /api/iosDevices/951 returned all 14 registered devices, byte-identical to the bare list (1284 bytes both ways) — the id segment is ignored. Worse than a 404 because it looks like it worked: anything taking the first element gets device 937 whatever it asked for. The DELETE shape the report also names was NOT probed; it would deregister a real phone.

Filed 13 Nov mid-investigation and wrong on its premise: it inferred 'the box stayed up, only the QuickApp engine restarted' from CPU jiffies in get_diagnostics. The HC3's own General settings showed uptime of 12 h that afternoon, i.e. a full reboot at 03:46. CPU counters are not an uptime signal. The cause was also not files failing to persist: disabled copier QA 4983 ran onInit on boot and copied 4953 over 4984 (see the finding at 1794582989). Kept, refuted, so nobody chases an engine-only restart.

Observed once, 13 Nov 2026 on 5.220.15: copier QA 4983 (enabled:false) ran onInit at boot and overwrote 4984 from 4953, files and variables; 4983 and 4953 since deleted, 4984 restored from the snapshot. Confirmed for that QA on that boot; NOT isolated whether every disabled QA runs onInit on boot. 4.34.0 puts the operational rule in the QuickApp guide (a one-off helper must delete or disarm itself) without claiming the general behaviour.

Snapshot now runs on the Pi (hc3-snapshot.timer) into /var/lib/hc3-mcp/snapshot, pushed to a private GitHub repo with secrets git-crypt-encrypted. 4.34.0 adds list_snapshots, get_snapshot_quickapp, diff_quickapp_vs_snapshot and restore_quickapp_from_snapshot, which read that repo server side; the 13 Nov restore becomes one diff and one restore call.

All three parts fixed in 4.34.0: set_quickapp_variables writes many with one PUT (one restart); set_quickapp_variable no longer points at modify_device, which rejects quickAppVariables by design; untyped variables are written as strings (true -> "true", 15 -> "15").
